lines: A singular subject takes a singular verb, and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
Find the real subject first. Phrases such as "of the applicants" or "along with her staff" describe the subject but do not change it.
The box of folders ___ on the shelf.
The subject is "box", which is singular. "Of folders" only describes it.
sections.answer: The box of folders is on the shelf.

lines: With "either ... or" and "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it: Either the clerks or the supervisor signs the logbook.
After a preposition such as to, for, with or between, use the object pronouns me, him, her, us and them.
As the subject of a verb, use I, he, she, we and they.
Cover the other person to check: "The memo was sent to Jose and (I / me)" becomes "sent to me", so the answer is me.
Treating "the number of" as plural. "The number of requests is rising" talks about one number, while "A number of requests are pending" means many requests.
Percent means "out of 100". To find a percent of a number, change the percent to a decimal and multiply.
What is 15% of 240?
Percent change compares the change with the original amount: change ÷ original × 100.
A price goes from ₱500 to ₱600. What is the percent increase?
A ratio compares parts. To share an amount in a ratio, add the parts, find the value of one part, then multiply.
Share ₱1,200 between two people in the ratio 1:3.
There are 1 + 3 = 4 parts, so one part is ₱1,200 ÷ 4 = ₱300.
In a proportion, the cross products are equal: if a/b = c/d, then a × d = b × c.
Successive percent changes multiply; they do not add. Raising a price by 20% and then lowering it by 20% gives 1.20 × 0.80 = 0.96, a 4% decrease, not "no change".
Successive discounts work the same way: 20% off and then 10% off is 0.80 × 0.90 = 0.72 of the price, a total of 28% off, not 30%.
After a 15% discount, a jacket costs ₱1,360. What was the original price?
The sale price is 85% of the original, so divide by 0.85 instead of adding 15% back.
Dividing by the new amount instead of the original. From ₱500 to ₱600 is a 20% increase, not 16.7%.
An analogy says that two pairs of words are related in the same way.
Put the relationship of the first pair into a short sentence, then pick the choice that fits the same sentence.
Pilot is to airplane as captain is to ___.
Relationship: a pilot is in command of an airplane.
A captain is in command of a ___.
Common relationships: worker and workplace, tool and its use, part and whole, opposites, words with the same meaning, cause and effect, and a unit and what it measures.
Reversing the order. In "Page is to book as ___ is to fence", the first word is the part and the second is the whole, so the answer is a part of a fence, such as a picket.
File a person's name by last name first, then first name, then middle name or initial: Cruz, Ana B.
"Nothing comes before something": a shorter name is filed before a longer name that starts the same way. Cruz comes before Cruzado, and Cruz, Ana comes before Cruz, Ana B.
Put in order: Reyes, Carla; Reyes, Carl; Reyes, Carmen.
The last names are the same, so compare the first names letter by letter: CARL, CARLA, CARMEN.
CARL ends first, and in the 4th letter L comes before M.
sections.answer: Reyes, Carl; Reyes, Carla; Reyes, Carmen

lines: Surname prefixes such as De la, Del and Delos are usually filed as one word, ignoring the spaces: De la Cruz is read as DELACRUZ.
Rules for abbreviations such as Sto. and Ma. differ between offices. In the exam, follow the rule given in the question.
Titles and suffixes do not change the order. Index "Dr. Ana Marie Tan" as Tan, Ana Marie (Dr.), and "Engr. Pablo Q. Ramos III" as Ramos, Pablo Q. III (Engr.).
A hyphenated surname is one unit: read Santos-Reyes as SANTOSREYES. "Nothing before something" still applies, so Reyes, Carlos comes before Reyes-Lim, Carla.
For businesses, move "The" to the end: The Manila Times becomes Manila Times, The. For government offices, start with the distinctive word: Department of Health becomes Health, Department of.
Straight numeric filing reads a number from left to right: 2024-0912 comes before 2025-0078.
Terminal-digit filing reads from the right: for 48-27-15, find section 15 first, then 27, then 48. It spreads new files evenly across the shelves.
In chronological filing, check whether the newest or the oldest item goes in front. Many offices keep the most recent document in front.

Filing systems: alphabetical by name; subject by topic, such as "Budget" or "Training"; geographic by place; numeric by an assigned number, which suits large files and keeps names private; chronological by date.
Filing by first name. "Ana Cruz" is filed under C for Cruz, not under A.

lessons.subject: General Information
lessons.title: The 1987 Constitution: Key Articles and Numbers

lines: The 1987 Constitution was ratified in a plebiscite on February 2, 1987. It has a Preamble and 18 Articles.
Article II: Declaration of Principles and State Policies
Article III: Bill of Rights
Article VI: Legislative Department
Article VII: Executive Department
Article VIII: Judicial Department
Article IX: Constitutional Commissions (Civil Service Commission, COMELEC, Commission on Audit)
Article X: Local Government
Article XI: Accountability of Public Officers

Terms of office: President, 6 years with no re-election. Vice President, 6 years, at most 2 successive terms. Senators, 6 years, at most 2 consecutive terms. House members, 3 years, at most 3 consecutive terms.
Minimum ages: President and Vice President 40, Senator 35, House member 25, voter 18.
Under Article IX-B, appointments in the civil service are based on merit and fitness, determined as far as practicable by competitive examination. That is the reason the Civil Service Exam exists.
Citizenship and suffrage: natural-born citizens are citizens of the Philippines from birth, without having to perform any act to acquire or perfect their citizenship (Article IV, Section 2).

To vote, a citizen must be at least 18 and must have lived in the Philippines for at least one year, and in the place where they will vote for at least six months, just before the election (Article V, Section 1).

Congress (Article VI): party-list representatives make up 20% of the House (Section 5(2)). A Senator must be natural-born, at least 35, able to read and write, a registered voter, and a resident for at least two years before the election (Section 3).
Congress opens its regular session on the fourth Monday of July (Section 15). A majority of each House is a quorum (Section 16(2)).
A pay raise for Senators and Representatives takes effect only after the full term of all the Members who approved it has ended (Section 10).

If the President dies, is permanently disabled, is removed or resigns, the Vice President becomes President. If both offices are vacant, the Senate President acts as President, then the Speaker of the House (Article VII, Section 8).
A candidate for President must have lived in the Philippines for at least ten years before the election (Article VII, Section 2).

Seven-year terms without reappointment: the Ombudsman (Article XI, Section 11) and the members of the Constitutional Commissions. The Commission on Audit and the Civil Service Commission each have a Chairman and two Commissioners; COMELEC has a Chairman and six. Justices of the Supreme Court retire at 70 (Article VIII, Section 11).

Other articles to know: Article I, National Territory. Article XII, National Economy: natural resources may be developed with corporations at least 60% Filipino-owned. Article XIII, Social Justice and Human Rights. Article XIV: Filipino and English are the official languages. Article XVI: the flag is red, white and blue, with a sun and three stars. Article XVII: amendments are ratified in a plebiscite held 60 to 90 days after approval.
Article II also says the separation of Church and State is inviolable (Section 6) and that the Philippines renounces war as an instrument of national policy (Section 2).
Congress wants to revoke a proclamation of martial law. What vote does it need?
Article VII, Section 18: Congress may revoke it by a vote of at least a majority of all its Members, voting jointly. The President cannot set the revocation aside.
sections.answer: A majority of all its Members, voting jointly

lines: Mixing up the term limits: Senators get 2 consecutive terms, House members 3, and the President cannot be re-elected at all.
Mixing up the residence rules: 10 years for President, 2 years for Senator, and for voters 1 year in the country plus 6 months in the place where they vote.
A synonym is a word with the same or nearly the same meaning. An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning.
Read the instruction carefully. "Closest in meaning" asks for a synonym, and "opposite in meaning" asks for an antonym.
Choose the word closest in meaning to "arduous".
An arduous task needs a lot of effort and is hard to finish. Look for the choice that means the same thing.
Choose the word opposite in meaning to "ascend".
To ascend is to go up, such as climbing stairs. The opposite is to go down.
In a vocabulary-in-context question, the sentence itself explains the word. Look at the words around it for clues such as an example, a reason or a contrast.
Replace the word with each choice. The right one keeps the meaning of the whole sentence.
The manager's terse reply was only three words long. What does "terse" mean?
The clue is "only three words long", so the reply was very short.
Word parts can help when a word is new to you. Pre- means before, post- means after, mal- means bad, and -less means without: a careless worker works without care.
Picking a word that is only related to the given word. "Tired" is related to "arduous" because hard work makes you tired, but it does not mean the same thing.
An idiom is a group of words whose meaning is different from the meaning of each word. You cannot work it out word by word; you have to learn it as a whole.
What does "to spill the beans" mean?
Nothing is really spilled. The "beans" stand for information someone was supposed to keep.
Many idioms come from everyday pictures. Thinking of the picture can help you remember the meaning.
"Under the weather" means slightly sick. "Once in a blue moon" means very rarely. "A piece of cake" means very easy.
After eight hours of meetings, the director said, "Let's call it a day."
She is speaking at the end of a long day of work, so she wants everyone to stop.
sections.answer: To stop working for the day

lines: When an idiom appears in a sentence, use the situation as your clue. Ask what the speaker most likely means at that moment.
"To see eye to eye" means to agree, so "The two offices finally saw eye to eye on the budget" means they reached an agreement.
Choosing the literal meaning. In the exam, a choice that describes the words exactly as written, such as actually spilling beans on the floor, is almost always wrong.
Read the questions first, then the passage. You will know what to look for as you read.
Every answer must come from the passage, not from what you already know about the topic.

Last year, a provincial hospital began sending text reminders to patients a day before their check-ups. Before this, about one in three patients missed their appointments. Within six months, missed appointments fell by half. The staff say the reminders cost very little, since the messages are sent automatically.
What is the passage mainly about? Every sentence is about the reminders and what they changed.
sections.answer: How text reminders reduced missed check-ups at a hospital

lines: A main idea question asks what the whole passage is about. A detail question asks for one fact the passage states directly, so find the exact line that says it.
In the passage above, a detail question could ask how many patients used to miss check-ups. The answer, about one in three, is stated in the second sentence.
An inference question asks what the passage suggests but does not say directly. The right answer is supported by the facts in the passage, not by a guess.
An author's purpose question asks why the writer included something, such as to explain, to give evidence, to persuade or to show a result.
Why does the passage mention that the reminders cost very little?
The passage already showed the reminders worked. Adding that they are cheap shows that the idea is easy to keep going.
sections.answer: To show that the reminders are an affordable solution

lines: For a vocabulary question, go back to the sentence with the word and read the sentences around it. The passage usually explains the word. For example, "automatically" here means the messages go out on their own, without staff typing each one.
Choosing an answer that is true but too narrow, or too broad. A main idea must cover the whole passage, not one detail, and it must not go beyond what the passage discusses.
In sentence completion, clue words tell you which way the meaning goes.
Although, despite, but and however signal a contrast. Because, since and so signal a cause or a result. And, also and a semicolon usually signal that the second part agrees with the first.
Although the road was ___, the bus still arrived on time.
"Although" signals a contrast. Arriving on time is good news, so the blank must be something that would normally cause a delay.
sections.answer: Although the road was flooded, the bus still arrived on time.

lines: Before looking at the choices, say your own word for the blank. Then pick the choice closest to it, and read the full sentence once more to check.
In paragraph completion, the missing sentence must continue the same topic and follow from the sentence before it. Watch for linking words such as as a result, for example and however.
In paragraph organization, first find the opening sentence. It introduces the person or the topic and does not depend on another sentence.
Then follow the links: time words such as first, then, after that and finally, and words that point back such as this, he, she or it.

Arrange: (A) Then she paid the fee at the cashier. (B) Lena went to the city hall to renew her business permit. (C) Finally, she received her new permit. (D) First, she lined up at the permits window.
B introduces Lena and her purpose, so it opens. The time words give the rest: First (D), Then (A), Finally (C).
Starting with a sentence that begins with a word like "then", "this" or "as a result". These words point back to something earlier, so that sentence cannot come first.
For time, use at for a clock time (at noon, at 3:30 p.m.), on for days and dates (on Friday, on May 12), and in for months, years and parts of the day (in August, in 2024, in the morning).
Use for with a length of time and since with a starting point: "She has lived here for ten months" but "She has lived here since January."
The training has been postponed ___ last week.
"Last week" is the point when the delay began, not a length of time.
sections.answer: The training has been postponed since last week.

lines: Some words always take the same preposition, so learn them as pairs: interested in, responsible for, capable of, comply with, depend on, different from.
Parallel structure means that items joined by and, or, but or not only ... but also have the same grammatical form.
If the first item is an -ing word, the others should be -ing words too. If the first is an adjective, the others should be adjectives.
Correct this sentence: The new clerk is fast, accurate, and has polite manners.
"Fast" and "accurate" are adjectives, but "has polite manners" is a verb phrase. Change it to an adjective.
sections.answer: The new clerk is fast, accurate, and polite.

lines: Mixing "to" verbs and -ing words in one list. "She likes to read, cooking, and to swim" should be "She likes reading, cooking, and swimming" or "She likes to read, cook, and swim."
Ang kasingkahulugan ay salitang pareho o halos pareho ang kahulugan. Ang kasalungat ay salitang kabaligtaran ang kahulugan.
Basahing mabuti ang tanong. Kapag "kasingkahulugan" o "kahulugan" ang hinihingi, hanapin ang katumbas. Kapag "kasalungat", hanapin ang kabaligtaran.
Ano ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang "marilag"?
Ginagamit ang marilag sa paglalarawan ng isang taong napakaganda, gaya ng "marilag na dalaga".
Ano ang kasalungat ng salitang "mapagbigay"?
Ang mapagbigay ay madaling magbahagi ng kanyang pag-aari. Ang kabaligtaran nito ay ayaw magbahagi.
Ang sawikain o idyoma ay pahayag na may kahulugang iba sa literal na kahulugan ng mga salita nito.
Halimbawa, ang "bukas-palad" ay taong matulungin at mapagbigay, at ang "ningas-kugon" ay taong magaling lamang sa simula at hindi tinatapos ang sinimulan.
Ilang ulit siyang pinaalalahanan ng kanyang ina, pero taingang kawali siya. Ano ang ibig sabihin ng "taingang kawali"?
Hindi tungkol sa tunay na tainga ang pahayag. Narinig niya ang paalala pero hindi niya ito pinansin.
Gamitin ang pangungusap bilang palatandaan. Ipalit ang bawat pagpipilian sa salita o sawikain, at piliin ang hindi nagbabago sa kahulugan ng buong pangungusap.
Pagpili ng literal na kahulugan ng sawikain. Ang "taingang kawali" ay hindi tumutukoy sa hugis ng tainga, kundi sa taong ayaw makinig.

lessons.subject: Verbal Ability
lessons.title: Filipino: Wastong Gamit ng mga Salita

lines: Ginagamit ang "ng" bago ang pangngalan, bilang tagatukoy ng layon o ng may-ari: "Bumili siya ng tinapay", "ang bag ng guro".

Ginagamit ang "nang" kapag sumasagot sa paano o kailan, kapag nangangahulugang upang, at sa pagitan ng inuulit na pandiwa: "Tumakbo siya nang mabilis", "Umalis siya nang dumating ako", "Kain nang kain".
Piliin ang wastong salita: Magsalita ka ___ malakas para marinig ng lahat.
Sinasagot ng "malakas" ang tanong na paano magsalita.
sections.answer: Magsalita ka nang malakas para marinig ng lahat.

lines: Gamitin ang "din" pagkatapos ng salitang nagtatapos sa katinig, at ang "rin" pagkatapos ng patinig o ng w at y: "Aalis din", "Sasama rin", "Ikaw rin".
Gamitin ang "may" kapag pangngalan, pandiwa o pang-uri ang kasunod: "May pulong". Gamitin ang "mayroon" kapag panghalip o kataga ang kasunod: "Mayroon kaming pulong", "Mayroon pa ba?"

Ang "kong" ay "ko" na may pang-angkop na -ng at ikinakabit sa kasunod na salita: "Gusto kong magpahinga." Ang "kung" ay pangatnig na nangangahulugang kapag o sakaling: "Tatawagan kita kung may balita."

Ginagamit ang -in kapag ang bagay mismo ang tinatanggal o ginagalaw, at ang -an kapag lugar, ibabaw o tao ang tinutukoy: "punasin ang alikabok", "punasan ang mesa"; "sabihin ang totoo", "sabihan si Ana".
May tatlong pangunahing aspekto ang pandiwa. Perpektibo kapag naganap na (kumain), imperpektibo kapag nagaganap o palagiang ginagawa (kumakain), at kontemplatibo kapag gagawin pa lamang (kakain).
Hanapin ang salitang pamanahon. Ang kahapon at kanina ay para sa perpektibo, ang ngayon at araw-araw ay para sa imperpektibo, at ang bukas, mamaya at sa susunod ay para sa kontemplatibo.
Piliin ang wastong salita: ___ kami sa Baguio sa susunod na linggo. (Pumunta, Pumupunta, Pupunta)
Ang "sa susunod na linggo" ay tumutukoy sa hinaharap, kaya kontemplatibo ang kailangan.
sections.answer: Pupunta kami sa Baguio sa susunod na linggo.

lines: Paggamit ng "ng" kapag paano ang sinasagot. Mali ang "Sumulat siya ng maayos"; ang tama ay "Sumulat siya nang maayos".
To add or subtract fractions, rewrite them over a common denominator, then add or subtract the numerators.
To multiply, multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms. To divide, flip the second fraction and multiply. Change mixed numbers such as 2 1/4 into improper fractions (9/4) first.
What is 5/8 ÷ 3/4?
Flip the second fraction and multiply: 5/8 × 4/3 = 20/24.
Simplify by dividing the top and bottom by 4.
To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points.

To multiply, multiply as if they were whole numbers, then count the decimal places in both factors. To divide by a decimal, move the decimal point to the right in both numbers until you are dividing by a whole number.
What is 3.6 ÷ 0.12?
Move both decimal points two places to the right: 360 ÷ 12.
To compare two fractions, cross-multiply. Is 5/7 or 7/10 larger? 5 × 10 = 50 and 7 × 7 = 49, so 5/7 is larger.
With several fractions, write them all over one common denominator, or change each to a decimal.
In word problems, "of" means multiply. When a fraction is taken "of what is left", work out what is left first, then take the fraction of that.
Rhea receives ₱24,000. She saves 1/3 of it and spends 1/4 of the rest on bills. How much is left?
Adding the tops and the bottoms. 1/2 + 1/3 is not 2/5. Over a common denominator it is 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.

lessons.subject: Numerical Ability
lessons.title: Order of Operations, Exponents and Roots

lines: Work in this order: parentheses first, then exponents, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right.
Many people remember it as PEMDAS.
Multiply and divide first: 6 × 2 = 12 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
Then work left to right: 20 − 12 + 3.
Parentheses: 3 + 5 = 8. Exponent: 2² = 4.
Multiply and divide: 8 × 4 = 32 and 10 ÷ 5 = 2.
Multiplication does not always come before division. They have equal rank, so go left to right: 24 ÷ 4 × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12, not 24 ÷ 8 = 3. The same goes for addition and subtraction.
An exponent tells how many times a number is multiplied by itself: 5³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.
A square root asks which number times itself gives the number: √49 = 7 because 7 × 7 = 49.
What is 4² − √81?
For the square root of a decimal, take the root of the digits and use half as many decimal places: √0.36 = 0.6 and √0.0025 = 0.05. Check by multiplying: 0.6 × 0.6 = 0.36.
Multiplying the base by the exponent. 3⁴ is 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81, not 3 × 4 = 12.
To solve an equation, do the same thing to both sides until x is alone. Undo addition and subtraction first, then multiplication and division.
If there are parentheses, multiply them out first: 3(x + 2) is 3x + 6.
If 4x + 9 = 37, what is x?
Subtract 9 from both sides: 4x = 28.
Divide both sides by 4.
Turn the words into an equation: "is" means =, "twice" means 2 ×, and "5 less than a number" means x − 5.
When a problem has two kinds of items and a total count, pretend all of them are the cheaper kind, then see how much extra the other kind adds.
Nico bought 15 notebooks, some at ₱30 and some at ₱45, for ₱525 in all. How many ₱45 notebooks did he buy?
If all 15 cost ₱30, he would pay ₱450.
Each ₱45 notebook adds ₱15, and ₱525 − ₱450 = ₱75, so 75 ÷ 15 = 5.
Consecutive numbers are written x, x + 1, x + 2. Consecutive even or odd numbers are x, x + 2, x + 4.
For three of them, the middle number is the sum ÷ 3. If three consecutive numbers add up to 72, the middle is 24, so they are 23, 24 and 25.
In age problems, use one letter for a present age and write the others from it. Add years to everyone for the future and subtract from everyone for the past.
The difference between two people's ages never changes.
Joel is 24 years older than his son. In 6 years, Joel will be 3 times as old as his son. How old is the son now?
Let the son be s, so Joel is s + 24. In 6 years: s + 30 = 3(s + 6).
s + 30 = 3s + 18, so 2s = 12 and s = 6. Check: in 6 years they are 36 and 12.
sections.answer: The son is 6 and Joel is 30

lines: Adding the years to only one person. If the problem says "in 6 years", both people are 6 years older.
If someone finishes a job in 5 hours, they do 1/5 of the job each hour. That fraction is their rate.
When people work together, add their rates. The time needed is 1 ÷ the combined rate.
Liza can encode a batch of records in 5 hours, and Joy can do it in 20 hours. How long will they take together?
Their rates are 1/5 and 1/20 of the batch per hour.
For two workers, together time = (a × b) ÷ (a + b). For 5 and 20 hours: 100 ÷ 25 = 4 hours.
When a crew of equal workers does a job, the job size is workers × days. More workers means fewer days, so divide the job by the new number of workers.
Four carpenters can build a shed in 15 days. How many days will 10 carpenters need?
The job is 4 × 15 = 60 carpenter-days.
A drain or leak works against you, so subtract its rate.
If people work together for a while and then one leaves, find the part already done, then divide what is left by the rate of whoever remains.
A faucet fills a drum in 3 hours, but a leak empties a full drum in 12 hours. How long does the empty drum take to fill?
Adding or averaging the times. Working together is always faster than the faster worker alone, so 5 hours and 20 hours together must be less than 5 hours.
Distance = rate × time. From this, rate = distance ÷ time and time = distance ÷ rate.
Write the time in hours when the speed is in km/h: 45 minutes is 0.75 hour.
A car travels at 80 km/h for 2 hours 15 minutes. How far does it go?
2 hours 15 minutes = 2.25 hours.
Moving in opposite directions, the gap grows by the sum of the speeds. Moving the same way, a faster vehicle catches up at the difference of the speeds.
For boats, downstream speed is boat + current and upstream speed is boat − current. The current is half the difference of the two.
A tricycle leaves the plaza at 7:00 a.m. at 30 km/h. A motorcycle follows on the same road at 7:30 a.m. at 50 km/h. When does the motorcycle catch up?
By 7:30 the tricycle is 30 × 0.5 = 15 km ahead.
The motorcycle gains 50 − 30 = 20 km each hour, so it needs 15 ÷ 20 = 0.75 hour, or 45 minutes.
To change km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6. To change m/s to km/h, multiply by 3.6. So 54 km/h is 15 m/s.
Average speed is total distance ÷ total time. It is not the average of the speeds, because more time is spent at the slower speed.
Mila drives 120 km to her province at 40 km/h and comes back on the same road at 60 km/h. What is her average speed?
Going takes 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours. Returning takes 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours.
Total: 240 km in 5 hours.
Writing minutes as decimals directly. 1 hour 20 minutes is not 1.2 hours; it is 1 20/60 = 1 1/3 hours.
The average (mean) is the sum of the values ÷ how many values there are.
Turning it around, the total is the average × the count. This is the key to finding a missing value.
Kim wants an average of 80 on six quizzes. Her first five scores are 75, 82, 78, 85 and 76. What does she need on the sixth?
Six quizzes averaging 80 total 6 × 80 = 480.
The five scores add up to 396.
In a weighted average, some values count more than others. Multiply each value by its weight or group size, add the results, then divide by the total weight.
A store sold 30 kg of rice at ₱50 per kg and 20 kg at ₱60 per kg. What was the average price per kilogram?
The total weight is 50 kg.
The median is the middle value after sorting from smallest to largest. With an even number of values, it is the average of the two middle values.
What is the median of 14, 3, 9, 21, 6 and 10?
Sorted: 3, 6, 9, 10, 14, 21. The two middle values are 9 and 10.
When someone joins or leaves a group, compare totals. If 4 people average 25 and a fifth joins to make the average 26, the new person is 5 × 26 − 4 × 25 = 130 − 100 = 30.
Taking the middle number without sorting first, or simply averaging two group averages when the groups are different sizes.
Simple interest = principal × rate × time, with the time in years. For months, use months ÷ 12.
The amount owed or saved at the end is principal + interest.
Mang Ben borrows ₱18,000 at 10% simple interest a year. How much interest does he owe after 9 months?
9 months is 9/12 of a year.
Rearrange the same formula to find the other parts: principal = interest ÷ (rate × time), and rate = interest ÷ (principal × time).
With compound interest, each period's interest is added to the balance and earns interest too. Multiply by (1 + rate) once per period.
Compounded semi-annually means half the yearly rate, twice a year. Quarterly means a quarter of the rate, four times a year.
₱5,000 is deposited at 6% compounded yearly. How much is in the account after 2 years?
After year 2: ₱5,300 × 1.06
Profit = selling price − cost. Percent profit or loss is based on the cost unless the problem says otherwise.
Selling at a 20% profit means the selling price is 120% of the cost. To find the cost from the selling price, divide by 1.20.
A store sells a rice cooker for ₱1,320 and makes a 20% profit on its cost. What did it cost the store?
The selling price is 120% of the cost.
Taking the percent of the selling price when it should be the cost. 20% off ₱1,320 is ₱1,056, which is not the cost.
Start by writing the difference between each pair of neighbors. If the differences are equal, keep adding that amount.
If the differences change, look at the differences themselves. They often grow by a fixed amount or double.
What comes next? 3, 4, 7, 12, 19, ...
The differences are 1, 3, 5, 7, growing by 2.
The next difference is 9, so 19 + 9.
If the numbers grow or shrink very fast, try dividing each number by the one before it. A series that multiplies or divides by the same number each time has a constant ratio.
What comes next? 2, 6, 18, 54, ...
Each number is 3 times the one before it.
Some series hide two patterns. Look at every other number, or check whether the steps take turns, such as add 3 then multiply by 2.
What comes next? 10, 1, 12, 3, 14, 5, ...
The 1st, 3rd and 5th numbers go 10, 12, 14 (add 2).
The 2nd, 4th and 6th go 1, 3, 5. The next number belongs to the first pattern.
Know the special series on sight: squares (1, 4, 9, 16), cubes (1, 8, 27, 64), and the series where each number is the sum of the two before it (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8).
Check in this order: differences, ratios, special series, then two patterns mixed together.
Choosing a rule that fits only the first two or three numbers. Test it on every number in the series before you answer.
Mixing does not create or destroy the pure ingredient. The amount of it before mixing equals the amount after.
Amount of ingredient = percent strength × total volume. For example, 8 liters of a 25% solution holds 0.25 × 8 = 2 liters of the ingredient.
How many liters of a 60% solution must be mixed with a 30% solution to make 15 liters of a 40% solution?
Let x be the liters of 60%, so 15 − x liters are 30%: 0.60x + 0.30(15 − x) = 0.40 × 15.
sections.answer: 5 liters of the 60% solution (and 10 liters of the 30%)

lines: Adding water changes the total but not the amount of the ingredient. Find the ingredient, then divide by the new percent to get the new total.
How much water must be added to 15 liters of a 40% juice concentrate to make it 25%?
The concentrate holds 0.40 × 15 = 6 liters of juice.
For 6 liters to be 25%, the total must be 6 ÷ 0.25 = 24 liters.
Price mixtures work the same way, with price × weight in place of percent × volume.
A rice dealer mixes rice at ₱60 per kg with rice at ₱48 per kg to make 40 kg worth ₱51 per kg. How many kilograms of the ₱60 rice does he use?
Let a be the kilograms of ₱60 rice: 60a + 48(40 − a) = 51 × 40.

Shortcut: the amounts are in the ratio of the distances from the target. From ₱48 to ₱51 is 3 and from ₱51 to ₱60 is 9, so the ₱60 rice and the ₱48 rice are used in the ratio 3:9, or 1:3. That gives 10 kg and 30 kg.
Answering with the final amount when the question asks how much to add. Read the last line again, and remember that the part you are not adding stays the same.

lessons.subject: Numerical Ability
lessons.title: Measurement: Area, Volume, Units and Time

lines: Perimeter is the distance around a shape, and area is the space inside it.
Rectangle: area = length × width, perimeter = 2 × (length + width). Square: area = side × side, perimeter = 4 × side. Triangle: area = 1/2 × base × height.
A classroom floor is 8 m long and 6 m wide. What are its area and perimeter?
Area = 8 × 6 = 48 square meters.
Perimeter = 2 × (8 + 6) = 28 meters.
For a circle, circumference = 2 × π × radius and area = π × radius × radius. Use π = 22/7 or 3.14.
With a radius of 7 cm and π = 22/7, the circumference is 44 cm and the area is 154 square cm.
Volume of a box = length × width × height. Volume of a cylinder = π × radius × radius × height.
1 cubic meter = 1,000 liters, and 1 liter = 1,000 cubic centimeters.
An aquarium is 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many liters does it hold when full?
Volume = 60 × 30 × 40 = 72,000 cubic cm.
Change everything to the same unit before you calculate. 1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 hour = 60 minutes, and 1 km/h = 1,000 m ÷ 3,600 seconds.
Larger unit to smaller, multiply. Smaller unit to larger, divide.
For time spans, count up to the next full hour, then the hours, then the leftover minutes. From 9:50 a.m. to 2:20 p.m. is 10 minutes + 4 hours + 20 minutes = 4 hours 30 minutes.
For days of the week, divide the number of days by 7 and count the remainder forward. If June 3 is a Tuesday, June 20 is 17 days later, which is 2 weeks and 3 days, so it is a Friday.
Using the diameter as the radius. The radius is half the diameter, so a 70 cm wide drum has a 35 cm radius.
The least common multiple (LCM) is the smallest number that all the given numbers divide into evenly.
Use it when things repeat on different schedules and you need the next time they happen together.
One jeepney route leaves the terminal every 12 minutes and another every 18 minutes. Both leave at 6:00 a.m. When do they next leave together?
Multiples of 18: 18, 36, 54. The first one that 12 also divides is 36.
The LCM is 36 minutes.
The greatest common factor (GCF) is the largest number that divides all the given numbers evenly.
Use it to split things into the largest number of equal groups, or the largest equal pieces, with nothing left over.
A teacher has 36 pencils and 60 pad papers. What is the greatest number of identical packs she can make with nothing left over?
Factors of 36 that also divide 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The greatest is 12.
Each pack gets 36 ÷ 12 = 3 pencils and 60 ÷ 12 = 5 pad papers.

With prime factors, the LCM takes every prime at its highest power and the GCF takes only the shared primes at their lowest power. For 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3², the LCM is 2² × 3² = 36 and the GCF is 2 × 3 = 6.
For two numbers, GCF × LCM = the two numbers multiplied: 6 × 36 = 12 × 18 = 216.
Using the wrong one. "Together again" and "leaves the same remainder" problems use the LCM. "Largest equal groups" problems use the GCF.

Statements with all, some and no describe groups. Picture each group as a circle: "All A are B" puts circle A inside circle B, "No A is B" keeps the circles apart, and "Some A are B" means at least one A is also a B.
A conclusion must be true in every picture that fits the statements, not just in the most likely one.
All cashiers are bonded. Some employees are not bonded. Which conclusion must be true?
Every cashier is inside the bonded group.
The employees who are not bonded are outside that group, so none of them can be a cashier.
Nothing is said about the bonded employees, so "some employees are cashiers" is not proven.
"If P, then Q" allows exactly two sure conclusions. If P happens, Q happens. If Q did not happen, P did not happen.
Knowing that Q happened, or that P did not happen, proves nothing. Q may have another cause.
Rule: If the generator is running, the lights are on.
The generator is running, so the lights are on. Valid.
The lights are off, so the generator is not running. Valid.
The lights are on: maybe the main power is back, so we cannot tell. The generator is off: the lights may still be on from the main power, so we cannot tell.
sections.answer: Only "running, so lights on" and "lights off, so not running" are certain.

lines: "Only P can do Q" means: if someone does Q, that person is P. It does not mean every P does Q.
"Not X unless Y" means: if X happens, then Y happened. Rewrite "only" and "unless" statements as if-then before you judge them.
No one gets a refund unless they show a receipt. Paolo showed a receipt. Must Paolo get a refund?
Rewrite: if a person gets a refund, that person showed a receipt.
Paolo showed a receipt. That is the "then" part, which proves nothing about the "if" part.
sections.answer: Not certain. A receipt is needed for a refund, but it does not guarantee one.

lines: To test a conclusion, try to imagine a case where every statement is true but the conclusion is false. If you can, the conclusion is not certain, and "cannot be determined" may be the answer.
"If P, then Q" means the same as "If not Q, then not P". This is the only safe way to turn an if-then statement around.
"No A are B" can be turned around: no B are A. "Some A are B" can too: some B are A. "All A are B" cannot.
To contradict "All A are B", it is enough that at least one A is not B. To contradict "No A is B", it is enough that some A is B.
A requirement is necessary but not always enough. "To be hired, you must pass the exam" does not mean everyone who passes is hired.
Ana says, "Ben is lying." Ben says, "Carlo is lying." Carlo says, "Ana and Ben are both lying." Who tells the truth?
Try each person as the truth-teller and look for a contradiction. If Ben is truthful, Carlo lies, and Ana (who says Ben lies) lies too. Carlo's claim that both lie is then false, which fits.
If Ana were truthful, Ben would lie, so Carlo would be truthful, but Carlo says Ana lies: a contradiction.
For day puzzles, find "today" first. "The day after tomorrow is Saturday" means today is Thursday, so yesterday was Wednesday.

Turning a statement around. "All cashiers are bonded" does not mean all bonded people are cashiers, and "If P, then Q" does not mean "If Q, then P". Concluding P because Q happened is called affirming the consequent, and it is invalid.
In a letter series, change each letter to its place in the alphabet (A = 1, B = 2, up to Z = 26), then look at the gaps between them.
The gaps may stay the same, grow by one each time, follow a number pattern such as squares, or two series may take turns.
What letter comes next? C, E, D, F, E, G, ...
As numbers: 3, 5, 4, 6, 5, 7.
The gaps take turns: +2, −1, +2, −1, +2. The next gap is −1.
7 − 1 = 6, which is F.
Remember EJOTY: E is 5th, J is 10th, O is 15th, T is 20th and Y is 25th. Count from the nearest one instead of from A.
In a mirror code (A↔Z, B↔Y), a letter and its mirror always add up to 27.

In a letter code, line up the word and its code letter by letter and find how far each letter moved. Check every letter, because the shift may be the same for all, grow letter by letter, or be a mirror or a reversal.
In a word code, a code word that appears in two phrases stands for the word the two phrases share.
If LAMP is written as NCOR, how is SIGN written in the same code?
L→N, A→C, M→O, P→R: every letter moves two places forward.
S→U, I→K, G→I, N→P.

Other codes to watch for: only the vowels change (A→E, E→I, I→O, O→U, U→A) while consonants stay; each letter is replaced by its number (A = 1); the word is written backward; or the code is the sum of the letter positions (SUN = 19 + 21 + 14 = 54).
When numbers stand for letters in a puzzle ("1 = R, 2 = E"), write the key down first, then decode one number at a time.
Forgetting to wrap around the alphabet. After Z comes A again, so Y moved three places forward is B (Z, A, B).
For ordering problems, draw a line, a row of seats or a stack of floors. Place the fixed facts first, such as "on the top floor" or "at the end", then add each comparison one at a time.
For a round table, each person's left and right are from that person's own view while facing the center.
Lorna is heavier than Mika. Nestor is lighter than Mika but heavier than Olive. Who is the second lightest?
From heaviest: Lorna, then Mika.
Nestor is below Mika and above Olive: Lorna, Mika, Nestor, Olive.
For a position in a line: total = position from the front + position from the back − 1. A person who is 5th from the front and 9th from the back is in a line of 13.
For directions, draw a compass with north at the top. A right turn goes clockwise (north, east, south, west) and a left turn goes the other way.
To find how far someone is from the start, cancel moves in opposite directions first. If movement is left in two directions at right angles, use a² + b² = c².
Tess walks 10 km west, then 6 km north, then 2 km east. How far is she from her starting point?
West and east partly cancel: 10 − 2 = 8 km west.
She is 8 km west and 6 km north of the start.
The sun rises in the east and sets in the west, and a shadow points away from the sun. In the afternoon, shadows point east.
In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows point west. If, just after sunrise, your shadow falls to your right, west is on your right, so you are facing south.
Common right triangles make distance questions quick: 3-4-5, 6-8-10 and 5-12-13.
Giving the total distance walked when the question asks how far the person is from the start. Tess walked 18 km, but she is only 10 km from where she began.
Read the title, labels and units of a table before the question. Then work out only what is asked, using the numbers from the right row or column.
Know which number to divide by. Part of a total: part ÷ total. A is what percent of B: A ÷ B. Percent change or percent more: (new − old) ÷ old.
An average is the total divided by the number of items.
Trainees per batch: Batch 1, 40; Batch 2, 50; Batch 3, 60; Batch 4, 50. Batch 2 had how many percent more trainees than Batch 1?
Difference: 50 − 40 = 10.
Compare with Batch 1, the one after "than": 10 ÷ 40 = 0.25.
Clinic X saw 200 patients, 30 of them children. Clinic Y saw 90 patients, 18 of them children. Which clinic had the larger share of children?
sections.answer: Clinic Y, even though Clinic X saw more children

lines: "Percent of" and "percent more" differ by 100. If A is 120% of B, then A is 20% more than B.
Dividing by the wrong number. In the batch example, 10 ÷ 50 gives 20%, which compares with Batch 2 instead of Batch 1. Also, a bigger count is not the same as a bigger rate.

lessons.subject: Analytical Ability
lessons.title: Classification: Finding the Odd One Out

lines: In classification, three choices share something and one does not. Find a short name for the group the three belong to, then the fourth is the answer.
Which one does not belong? Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao, Cebu
Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao are the three main island groups of the Philippines.
Cebu is a province inside the Visayas, not an island group.
Which number does not belong? 15, 21, 27, 32
15, 21 and 27 are all odd and can be divided by 3.
32 is even and cannot be divided by 3.
Groups to check: kind (animal, plant, food), use or job, a part versus a whole, a tool versus what the tool works on, and level, such as local versus national.
For numbers, check even and odd, prime numbers, multiples, squares and cubes.

Choosing the first difference you notice, such as the longest word. Check that your rule fits exactly three choices and leaves out only one. If two rules work, the one about meaning or use is usually the intended answer.
Many office words are hard because of double letters. Learn them in parts: com-mit-tee has a double m, a double t and a double e. Em-bar-rass has a double r and a double s.
Some words double only one letter: recommend has one c and a double m, and occasion has a double c and one s.
Which word is spelled correctly: Comittee, Committee, Commitee or Comitee?
Break it into parts: com-mit-tee.
Each part doubles its consonant, and the word ends in a double e.

When you add -ed or -ing to a word that ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the last consonant if the stress is on the last part of the word: begin becomes beginning, refer becomes referred, omit becomes omitted.
If the stress is not on the last part, do not double: offer becomes offered, and benefit becomes benefited.

For words ending in -ance or -ence, look for a related word ending in -ant or -ent. The vowel stays the same: assistant and assistance, attendant and attendance, competent and competence, independent and independence.
With the "ee" sound, ie is the usual order: believe, achieve, field, brief. Right after c, ei is usual: conceive, perceive.
A few common words break this pattern, such as seize, weird and either, so learn those by sight.
Other office words that are often misspelled: government (the n before m), February (the r after b), calendar (ends in -ar), schedule, privilege (no d), and definitely (ends in -itely).
Spelling a word the way it is said in quick speech. People often say "goverment" and "Febuary", but the written words keep every letter: government and February.
Comparison items test whether you notice one small difference. Never read the whole item at a glance; check it in small pieces, from left to right.
First check the length. If one number has more digits or one name has more letters, the pair is already different.
For numbers, split long strings into groups of three or four and compare group by group. The most common trick is two digits swapping places, such as 365 and 356.
Also check dashes, letters inside codes, and the last digit, which is easy to skip.
Are these the same? 8143-0927-55 and 8143-0972-55
First group: 8143 and 8143 match.
Second group: 0927 and 0972. The last two digits are swapped.

For names, check the first name, the middle initial and the last name separately. Look out for one changed vowel (Manalo and Manalu), a doubled letter (Bautista and Bauttista) and look-alike middle initials such as O and Q, or M and N.

For addresses, check the house or unit number, the street name, the street type (St., Ave., Rd.), the barangay and the city, in that order. A changed abbreviation makes two addresses different even if everything else matches.
Are these the same? 88 Rizal Ave., Brgy. San Roque, Pasig City and 88 Rizal St., Brgy. San Roque, Pasig City
Number: 88 and 88 match. Street name: Rizal and Rizal match.
Street type: Ave. and St. do not match.
sections.answer: Not the same: Ave. differs from St.

lines: When a question asks how many pairs are the same, mark each pair as you go, same or different, then count your marks. Do not try to keep the count in your head.
Stopping after the first part that matches. Two names can share the same first and last name and still differ in the middle initial, so check every part to the end.

A business letter has its parts in this order: the heading or letterhead with the sender's details, the date, the inside address with the receiver's name and address, the salutation such as "Dear Ms. Reyes:", the body, the complimentary close, and the signature with the typed name and position.
Notations go at the bottom, below the signature: "Encl." means something is sent with the letter, and "cc" lists the people who receive a copy.

A memorandum, or memo, is for messages inside an office or agency. It starts with the lines TO, FROM, DATE and SUBJECT, then goes straight to the message. It has no inside address, no salutation and no complimentary close.

Incoming mail is handled in steps. The receiving clerk stamps each document with the date and time it arrived and who received it, records it in the incoming logbook, then routes it to the right office.
A routing slip shows who must see or act on a document, and in what order. Mail marked "Confidential" or "Personal" is logged but delivered unopened to the person named.
A clerk at a city hall receives a letter for the Human Resource Office. What does she do, in order?
She stamps it to show when it was received and by whom.
She enters it in the incoming logbook.
She attaches a routing slip and sends it on.
Good office practice also covers phone calls and meetings. When the person a caller wants is not free, take a complete message: the caller's name, number, purpose, and the date and time of the call.
The agenda lists the topics before a meeting. The minutes are the written record of what was discussed and decided.
A tickler file is a reminder file arranged by date. Each morning the clerk opens that day's folder to see which follow-ups and deadlines are due.

Records management: a retention schedule lists how long each kind of record is kept before it may be disposed of. Records with lasting legal or historical value, such as laws and ordinances, are kept permanently.
Government records may be disposed of only with the authority of the National Archives of the Philippines (RA 9470). Confidential records may be copied and handled only by authorized staff.
Clear, consistent folder labels let anyone find a record quickly. For supplies, use FIFO: first in, first out, so older stock is used first.

More letter parts: an attention line, such as "Attention: Records Officer", sends a letter addressed to an office to a particular person. Reference initials such as "JDC:mrs" show who wrote the letter (JDC) and who typed it (mrs).
Formal business letters put a colon after the salutation ("Dear Mr. Santos:"), and letters to officials close with "Respectfully yours" or "Very truly yours".
Mixing up "Encl." and "cc". "Encl." is about an attachment sent with the letter, while "cc" is about other people who get a copy.
For a purchase, multiply each item's price by its quantity, then add the amounts. To find the change or the amount left, subtract the total from the money given or the fund.
A clerk buys 3 reams of bond paper at ₱245 each and 5 boxes of staple wire at ₱38.50 each. She pays with ₱1,000. How much change does she get?
To find the cost of one item, divide the total by the number of items: 12 folders for ₱186 cost ₱186 ÷ 12 = ₱15.50 each.
For work done over time, multiply the rate by the working hours. Subtract any break before multiplying.
A clerk files 25 folders an hour. She works from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with a one-hour lunch break. How many folders does she file?
8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. is 8 hours. Minus the 1-hour break leaves 7 working hours.
When items are numbered from one number to another, including both, subtract and then add 1.
Official receipts are numbered from 1201 to 1280, including both. How many receipts are there?
Add 1 because both the first and the last receipt are counted.
Estimate first, then check. ₱927.50 is close to ₱1,000, so a small amount of change, like ₱72.50, makes sense.
Forgetting the break or the extra 1. A workday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with lunch has 7 working hours, not 8, and receipts 1201 to 1280 are 80, not 79.
The 1987 Constitution divides power among three branches, so that no single branch holds all of it.
Legislative (Article VI): Congress makes the laws.
Executive (Article VII): the President carries out the laws.
Judicial (Article VIII): the Supreme Court and the lower courts interpret the laws and settle legal disputes.
Congress has two Houses: the Senate, with 24 Senators elected at large (Article VI, Section 2), and the House of Representatives.

Appropriation, revenue and tariff bills, bills increasing the public debt, bills of local application and private bills must start in the House. The Senate may propose or concur with amendments (Article VI, Section 24).
The people themselves can propose and enact laws through initiative and referendum (Article VI, Section 32).
A bill becomes law in one of three ways (Article VI, Section 27):
The President signs it.
The President does not communicate a veto within 30 days of receiving it.
The President vetoes it, and each House, voting separately, passes it again by two-thirds of all its Members.
The President is Commander-in-Chief of all armed forces and may declare martial law for no more than 60 days, which Congress may revoke or extend (Article VII, Section 18).

The President grants reprieves, commutations and pardons after conviction by final judgment, except in impeachment cases. Amnesty also needs the concurrence of a majority of all the Members of Congress (Article VII, Section 19).
A treaty is valid only if at least two-thirds of all the Senators concur (Article VII, Section 21).
The Supreme Court has a Chief Justice and 14 Associate Justices, 15 members in all (Article VIII, Section 4).

The President appoints them from a list of at least three nominees from the Judicial and Bar Council for each vacancy, with no confirmation by the Commission on Appointments (Article VIII, Section 9).
A Senator wants to file a new tax bill in the Senate first. Can the bill start there?
A tax bill is a revenue bill, and revenue bills must originate exclusively in the House (Article VI, Section 24). The Senate can only propose or concur with amendments.
sections.answer: No. It must start in the House of Representatives.

lines: Congress, in joint public session, canvasses the votes for President and Vice President, and the Supreme Court sitting en banc is the sole judge of contests over those elections (Article VII, Section 4).

Impeachment: the House initiates, the Senate tries and decides (Article XI, Section 3). When the President is on trial, the Chief Justice presides but does not vote, and conviction needs two-thirds of all the Senators.
Mixing up the two-thirds votes. A veto override needs two-thirds of each House voting separately, but a treaty needs only the Senate, with two-thirds of all its Members.

lessons.subject: General Information
lessons.title: RA 6713: Code of Conduct for Public Officials

lines: RA 6713 is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. The Civil Service Commission has primary responsibility for administering and enforcing it (RA 6713, Section 12).
The eight norms of conduct (RA 6713, Section 4):
Commitment to public interest
Professionalism: excellence, intelligence and skill, without being seen as dispensers or peddlers of undue patronage
Justness and sincerity
Political neutrality: service to everyone regardless of party affiliation
Responsiveness to the public
Nationalism and patriotism
Commitment to democracy
Simple living: modest lives, with no extravagant display of wealth
Letters and requests from the public must be answered within 15 working days from receipt (RA 6713, Section 5(a)).
Prohibited acts under RA 6713, Section 7:
Having a financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their office (Section 7(a)).
Practicing their profession in connection with any matter before their former office within one year after leaving it (Section 7(b)).
Disclosing or misusing confidential information known to them by reason of their office (Section 7(c)).
Soliciting or accepting gifts in the course of official duties or in connection with any transaction their office may affect (Section 7(d)).
An unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value, not given in anticipation of or in exchange for a favor, does not count as a gift (Section 3(c)).
The SALN, or Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth, is filed under oath (RA 6713, Section 8).
When: within 30 days of taking office, on or before April 30 every year, and within 30 days of leaving office.
Whose: the official, the spouse, and unmarried children under 18 living in the household (Section 8(A)).
Officials must also disclose their relatives in government within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity (Section 8(B)).
A newly appointed official is a director of a private company and owns shares in it, and the company deals with her office. What must she do, and by when?
RA 6713, Section 9 gives two separate deadlines counted from assuming office: one for the position and one for the shares.
sections.answer: Resign as director within 30 days and divest the shares within 60 days.

lines: Swapping the Section 9 deadlines. Resigning from the private position comes first, within 30 days; divesting the shares comes later, within 60 days.
The UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on December 10, 1948, which is why Human Rights Day is December 10.
Its Article 1 says: "All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights."
In the Philippines, the Commission on Human Rights, created under Article XIII of the 1987 Constitution, investigates human rights violations.
Bill of Rights (Article III) items the exam often asks about:
No person shall be twice put in jeopardy of punishment for the same offense (Section 21).
A person under investigation must be told of the right to remain silent and to have competent and independent counsel, preferably of his own choice (Section 12(1)).
The people have the right to information on matters of public concern (Section 7).
The writ of habeas corpus is the remedy against illegal detention: the detained person is brought before a court so the legality of the detention can be examined.
Treaties: the Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) covers everyone under 18, and CEDAW protects the rights of women.
Women: RA 9262, Anti-VAWC Act (2004); RA 9710, Magna Carta of Women (2009); RA 11313, Safe Spaces Act or "Bawal Bastos" law (2019).
Children: RA 7610, Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination (1992); RA 9344, Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act.

Others: RA 8371, Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act (1997); RA 7277, Magna Carta for Persons with Disability (1992); RA 9994, Expanded Senior Citizens Act (2010); RA 9208, Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act (2003); RA 9745, Anti-Torture Act (2009).

Under RA 9344, a child 15 or below at the time of the offense is exempt from criminal liability but goes through an intervention program. A child above 15 and below 18 is also exempt unless he acted with discernment.
Under RA 9994, Section 4, senior citizens (60 and above) get a 20% discount and VAT exemption on covered goods and services such as medicines.
Under RA 8371, Section 3(g), free and prior informed consent must be secured from an indigenous community before activities affecting its ancestral domain.
A stranger catcalls a woman on the street. Which law covers this: RA 7877 or RA 11313?
RA 7877 (1995) covers harassment by persons in authority at work or school. RA 11313 covers harassment by anyone, including strangers, in streets, public places, online and at work.
Peace in Mindanao: the government signed an agreement with the MNLF in 1996, and the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro with the MILF in 2014.
The 2014 agreement led to RA 11054 (2018), the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
RA 9851 (2009) penalizes crimes against international humanitarian law, genocide and other crimes against humanity.
More Bill of Rights sections that the exam asks about:
Section 2: only a judge may issue a search warrant or warrant of arrest, after personally examining the complainant and witnesses under oath.
Section 3(2): evidence obtained through an illegal search or a violation of the privacy of communication is inadmissible for any purpose in any proceeding.
Section 9: private property shall not be taken for public use without just compensation.

Section 13: everyone has the right to bail before conviction, except those charged with offenses punishable by reclusion perpetua when the evidence of guilt is strong. The right to bail is not impaired even when the writ of habeas corpus is suspended.
Section 14: the accused is presumed innocent until the contrary is proved.
Section 15: the writ of habeas corpus may be suspended only in cases of invasion or rebellion, when public safety requires it.
Section 18: no person shall be detained solely by reason of political beliefs and aspirations.
Section 20: no person shall be imprisoned for debt or non-payment of a poll tax.
Section 22: no ex post facto law or bill of attainder shall be enacted. Article III has 22 sections in all.
A new law punishes an act that was legal when it was done. Which part of the Bill of Rights does it violate?
A law that makes a past act a crime, or punishes it more heavily after the fact, is an ex post facto law (Article III, Section 22).
sections.answer: The ban on ex post facto laws

lines: More rights laws by number: RA 7877, Anti-Sexual Harassment Act (1995). RA 10354, Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act (2012). RA 10627, Anti-Bullying Act (2013). RA 10754, 20% discount and VAT exemption for persons with disability (2016). RA 10931, free tuition in state and local universities and colleges (2017). RA 11036, Mental Health Act (2018). RA 11166, Philippine HIV and AIDS Policy Act (2018). RA 11596, ban on child marriage (2021). RA 11648, age of sexual consent raised to 16 (2022). RA 11861, Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act (2022). RA 11930, against online sexual abuse and exploitation of children (2022).

The UDHR has 30 articles. Together with the two covenants of 1966, the ICCPR (civil and political rights, such as free speech and voting) and the ICESCR (economic, social and cultural rights, such as work and education), it forms the International Bill of Human Rights. The Convention against Torture was adopted in 1984.

The Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU) leads the peace process. The Bangsamoro Organic Law was ratified in plebiscites in 2019, and BARMM replaced the ARMM.
RA 11188 (2019) protects children in situations of armed conflict. International humanitarian law requires parties to distinguish civilians from combatants (the principle of distinction).

The International Day of Peace is September 21, and September is National Peace Consciousness Month. The UN Sustainable Development Goals, 17 goals for 2030, include SDG 16: peace, justice and strong institutions.
Mixing up RA 9262 and RA 9710. RA 9262 penalizes violence against women and their children; RA 9710 is the Magna Carta of Women.
Mixing up the MNLF and the MILF. The 1996 agreement was with the MNLF; the 2014 agreement behind the Bangsamoro law was with the MILF.
Thinking that a suspended writ of habeas corpus also removes the right to bail. Article III, Section 13 says the right to bail is not impaired even then.
The State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology (Article II, Section 16).
Sustainable development means meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs (Brundtland Report, Our Common Future, 1987).
Environment laws by number:
RA 8749: Clean Air Act of 1999
RA 9275: Clean Water Act of 2004
RA 9003: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
RA 9147: Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001
RA 6969: Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1990
RA 7586: NIPAS Act of 1992, expanded by RA 11038 in 2018
RA 8550: Fisheries Code of 1998, amended by RA 10654 in 2015
RA 7942: Mining Act; PD 705: Revised Forestry Code
RA 9729: Climate Change Act of 2009, which created the Climate Change Commission

RA 9003 requires waste to be segregated at the source, such as homes and offices, before collection. Materials Recovery Facilities receive and sort recyclable and compostable waste so it does not go to disposal sites.
The waste hierarchy puts prevention and reduction at the source first, then reuse and recycling, then recovery, with disposal last.
Under PD 1586, a project that may harm the environment needs an Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) from the DENR Environmental Management Bureau before it proceeds.
The greenhouse effect is the trapping of heat by gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapor. Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels is the biggest contributor to human-caused warming.
The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to keep warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and to try to limit it to 1.5°C.
El Niño usually brings below-normal rainfall and drought to the Philippines; La Niña usually brings above-normal rainfall (PAGASA).
A choice says the Montreal Protocol was made to cut greenhouse gases. Is that right?
The Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out ozone-depleting chemicals such as CFCs. Greenhouse gases are handled by the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement.
sections.answer: No. The Montreal Protocol protects the ozone layer.

lines: RA 10121, the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010, created the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC).
The Secretary of National Defense chairs the NDRRMC; the DILG, DSWD, DOST and NEDA Secretaries are Vice Chairpersons; and the Office of Civil Defense is the secretariat (RA 10121, Section 5).
Dates: World Water Day is March 22, Earth Day is April 22, and World Environment Day is June 5.
Biodiversity is the variety of life within species, between species and of ecosystems (Convention on Biological Diversity, Article 2).

Under RA 10121, each local government sets aside not less than 5% of its estimated revenue from regular sources as the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund. Thirty percent of that fund is a Quick Response Fund for relief and recovery.
The DSWD Secretary is the vice chair for disaster response. July is National Disaster Resilience Month (Executive Order No. 29, s. 2017). The Fire Code of the Philippines is RA 9514 (2008).

Know which agency does what: PHIVOLCS (under the DOST) monitors volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis. PAGASA (also under the DOST) handles weather, tropical cyclone wind signals and rainfall warnings, where yellow, orange and red rise in seriousness and red calls for evacuation in flood-prone areas.
A storm surge is an abnormal rise of seawater pushed onshore by a storm's winds. Mangroves soften storm surges and protect coasts from erosion.

During an earthquake indoors: drop, cover and hold on. If the sea suddenly pulls back after a strong quake, move to higher ground at once, because a tsunami may follow. Keep a go bag with supplies for at least 72 hours.

More environment laws: RA 9512, Environmental Awareness and Education Act (2008). RA 10771, Philippine Green Jobs Act (2016). RA 11898, Extended Producer Responsibility Act (2022), which makes large companies recover their plastic packaging waste.

The Kyoto Protocol (1997) set binding greenhouse gas targets for developed countries. The ozone layer absorbs most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays. Food scraps and peelings are biodegradable; plastic, glass and cans are not.

Treating the ozone hole and global warming as one problem. Ozone thinning comes from chemicals such as CFCs (Montreal Protocol); global warming comes from greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (Paris Agreement).
Mixing up PAGASA and PHIVOLCS. PAGASA is for weather and typhoons; PHIVOLCS is for volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis.
Public office is a public trust (Article XI, Section 1). Several laws turn this principle into rules against corruption and red tape.
Good government laws by number:
RA 3019 (1960): Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act
RA 6713: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
RA 6770: law on the Office of the Ombudsman
RA 7080: Anti-Plunder Act
RA 7160: Local Government Code of 1991
RA 10173: Data Privacy Act of 2012
RA 11032 (2018): Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act
RA 12009 (2024): New Government Procurement Act, which replaced RA 9184
RA 11032 amended RA 9485, the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007, and created the Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA).
Maximum processing times (RA 11032, Section 9(b)): 3 working days for simple transactions, 7 for complex ones, and 20 for highly technical ones.
Every office must post a Citizen's Charter showing, step by step, its services, requirements, fees and processing times.
A permit application is classified as complex. What is the longest the office may take to process it?
RA 11032, Section 9(b): simple 3, complex 7, highly technical 20 working days.
The Office of the Ombudsman investigates complaints against public officials and employees and prosecutes those found liable (Article XI, Sections 12 and 13; RA 6770).
Plunder is amassing ill-gotten wealth of at least ₱50 million in total (RA 7080, Section 2, as amended by RA 7659).
The National Privacy Commission, created by RA 10173, enforces the Data Privacy Act.
In government procurement, public competitive bidding is the general rule under both RA 9184 and RA 12009. Direct contracting, negotiated procurement and shopping are allowed only in specific cases.
Executive Order No. 2, s. 2016 put Freedom of Information into effect in the Executive Branch, based on the right to information in Article III, Section 7.
RA 11032 also sets a zero-contact policy: apart from the preliminary assessment of a request, processing staff should have no contact with applicants. This cuts the chances for fixing and bribery.
The Commission on Audit examines and audits government funds and property (Article IX-D). The Sandiganbayan is the special court for graft and corruption cases of public officials.

More laws by number: RA 9470, National Archives of the Philippines Act (2007), on keeping and disposing of public records. RA 10149, GOCC Governance Act (2011). RA 10175, Cybercrime Prevention Act (2012). RA 10667, Philippine Competition Act (2015). RA 11223, Universal Health Care Act (2019).

The passing rating in the Civil Service Examination is 80. Sub-Professional eligibility covers first-level positions, such as clerical and trades work. Professional eligibility covers first- and second-level positions.
Presidential Decree No. 907 grants civil service eligibility to college honor graduates.
Mixing up RA 3019 and RA 6713. RA 3019 penalizes graft and corrupt practices; RA 6713 sets the norms of conduct and the SALN rules.
Calling RA 9184 the current procurement law. RA 12009 replaced it in 2024.
Probability = number of ways to get what you want ÷ total number of possible outcomes. Simplify the fraction at the end.
A jar holds 5 red, 3 yellow and 4 green candies. One is picked at random. What is the probability that it is yellow?
There are 5 + 3 + 4 = 12 candies, and 3 are yellow.
For two things that must both happen, multiply their probabilities.
If the first item is not put back, there is one fewer item for the second pick, so change the counts before the second step.
The names of 4 men and 6 women are in a box. Two names are drawn without putting the first back. What is the probability that both are women?
First draw: 6/10. Then 5 women are left out of 9, so the second draw is 5/9.
When order does not matter, as in choosing a committee, count the choices in order, then divide by the number of ways to arrange the chosen people.
3 people can be arranged in 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways, and 2 people in 2 × 1 = 2 ways.
In how many ways can 3 delegates be chosen from 7 barangay officials?
Each group of 3 is counted 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 times.
The probability that something does not happen is 1 minus the probability that it does. If the chance of yellow is 1/4, the chance of not yellow is 3/4.
Two dice give 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes. A sum of 7 happens 6 ways (1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1), so its probability is 6/36 = 1/6.
When order matters, multiply the choices: 4 different books can be arranged in 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 ways.
Handshakes are pairs, so order does not matter: with 8 people there are (8 × 7) ÷ 2 = 28 handshakes.
Keeping the same counts on the second draw when the first item was not put back. Without replacement, both the favorable count and the total go down.
Commission = commission rate × sales. If there is a base pay, add it to the commission.
Read carefully: some plans pay commission only on sales above a quota, so subtract the quota from the sales first.
Joy sells insurance and earns an 8% commission. This month she sold ₱45,000. How much is her commission?
VAT in the Philippines is 12%. To add it to a price, multiply by 1.12: ₱1,500 becomes ₱1,680.
To find the price before VAT from a total that already includes it, divide by 1.12.
A receipt shows ₱3,360, which already includes 12% VAT. How much of it is VAT?
Price before VAT: ₱3,360 ÷ 1.12 = ₱3,000.
A unit rate is the price for one unit, such as one kilogram or 100 mL. Divide the price by the quantity, then compare the unit rates to find the better buy.
A 1-liter bottle of cooking oil costs ₱95 and a 350 mL bottle costs ₱35. Which is cheaper per 100 mL, and by how much?
1 liter = 1,000 mL, so the big bottle costs ₱95 ÷ 10 = ₱9.50 per 100 mL.
The small bottle costs ₱35 ÷ 3.5 = ₱10.00 per 100 mL.
The VAT inside a VAT-inclusive total is total × 12 ÷ 112. For ₱3,360: 3,360 × 12 ÷ 112 = ₱360.
Taking 12% of a total that already includes VAT. That charges tax on the tax and gives too large an answer.
A clock face is 360°, so each hour mark is 30° apart. The minute hand moves 6° per minute.
The hour hand also moves: 30° per hour plus 0.5° per minute. Angle between the hands = (30 × hours) − (5.5 × minutes), ignoring any minus sign. If the result is more than 180°, subtract it from 360°.
What is the angle between the hands at 4:20?
120 − 110 = 10. Check: the minute hand is at 120° and the hour hand has moved past 4 to 130°.
What is the smaller angle between the hands at 2:45?
30 × 2 = 60 and 5.5 × 45 = 247.5, so the difference is 187.5°.
That is more than 180°, so take 360° − 187.5°.
Only on the hour does the hour hand point exactly at a number. At 3:00 the angle is 90°, but at any time after 3:00 the hour hand has moved toward 4.
For a table or chart, first find exactly what is asked: one value, a total, a difference, an average or a percent.
Percent of a whole = part ÷ total × 100. Every row counts in a total or average, including rows with zero.
A school canteen sold 64 rice meals, 40 pancit, 32 turon and 24 drinks in one day. What percent of the items sold were rice meals?
Treating the hour hand as fixed on the number, or leaving a zero value out of an average. Both give a wrong answer that is often one of the choices.
Break a long description into small steps, starting from the person the speaker knows best, usually "my". Replace each phrase with a simpler word: "my mother's brother" becomes "my uncle".
Draw a small family tree. Put each generation on its own row, connect parents to children with lines, and mark each person as male or female.
Pointing to a man, Liza says, "He is the son of my mother's only brother." How is the man related to Liza?
My mother's only brother is Liza's uncle.
The son of Liza's uncle is the child of her parent's sibling.
Ramon is Tina's father. Tina is Joey's sister. Carlo is Joey's son. How is Ramon related to Carlo?
Tina and Joey are siblings, so Ramon is Joey's father too.
Carlo is Joey's son, so Ramon is the father of Carlo's father.
Parent's brother: uncle. Parent's sister: aunt. Sibling's child: nephew or niece. Parent's sibling's child: cousin. Spouse's parent: father-in-law or mother-in-law. Son's wife: daughter-in-law.
Ignoring the speaker's gender. "My mother's only son" is the speaker's brother if the speaker is a woman, but it is the speaker himself if the speaker is a man.

Capitalize the first word of a sentence and every proper noun: names of people, agencies, offices, places, days of the week, months and holidays. Examples are Department of Education, Iloilo City, Thursday, June and Independence Day.
Common nouns such as memo, office, employee and form stay in small letters.
A title is capitalized when it comes right before a name: Director Santos, Mayor Dela Cruz. Used alone, it is usually written in small letters: the director signed the memo.
Fix the capitals: the regional director of the department of health will visit cebu city in august.
Capitalize the first word, the agency name, the city and the month.
"Regional director" is not followed by a name, so it stays in small letters.
sections.answer: The regional director of the Department of Health will visit Cebu City in August.

lines: Use a comma to separate items in a series, after an introductory phrase such as "After the meeting,", and before and, but or so when they join two complete sentences.
A semicolon joins two complete sentences without a joining word. A colon comes after a complete statement to introduce a list or an explanation.
Punctuate: The forms arrived on Tuesday but the clerk has not checked them yet.
"The forms arrived on Tuesday" and "the clerk has not checked them yet" are both complete sentences.
They are joined by "but", so a comma goes before it.
sections.answer: The forms arrived on Tuesday, but the clerk has not checked them yet.

lines: Use an apostrophe to show ownership: the employee's leave form for one employee, and the employees' lounge for many.
Putting a colon right after a verb. Write "The requirements are a birth certificate and a valid ID" with no colon after "are". Use a colon only when the words before it form a complete sentence.
